title: Osho on the Witness Behind the Mind
description: What Osho taught about the witness, in plain words. You are not your thoughts. Then who is it that sees them? A rope mistaken for a snake, a mirror that never gathers dust, two birds sitting on one tree, an actor who forgets he is acting, and Chuang Tzu waking from his butterfly dream. Then a meditation to rest as the one who watches.

chapters.title: Osho on the Witness Behind the Mind
chapters.ref: Osho, My Way: The Way of the White Clouds

beats.say: You say: I am angry. I am sad. I am worried. But have you ever stopped and asked... who is it that knows the anger? Who is watching the sadness?
The anger comes and goes. The sadness comes and goes. But the one who sees them... has never come and never gone.
The old seers of India called it the witness. Osho made it the heart of his teaching. Not the thoughts, not the feelings, but the light in which they appear.
He gave a simple hint: "Find moments when you are not, and those will be the moments when you will be for the first time...really." Tonight we look for this witness. Not in books. In you.
A man is walking home through the village at night. There is no moon. And on the path in front of him, he sees a snake.
His heart starts pounding. He cannot move. Sweat runs down his face. He can almost see the snake moving, ready to strike.
Then someone comes from the other side with a lantern. And in the light, the man sees... it is only a rope. An old piece of rope lying on the path.
Now tell me. Where did the snake go? Did it run away? No. It was never there. Only the darkness made it.
This is the whole of our misery. We take the mind for ourselves. We take the fears for reality. We are running from snakes that are only ropes.
Osho taught: don't fight the darkness, bring light. You don't have to kill the snake. You have to bring the lamp. And the lamp is awareness.
In an old Chinese monastery the master was getting old, and he wanted to choose who would come after him. So he said: Write me a poem that shows what you have understood.
The head monk wrote on the wall: The body is a tree, the mind is a bright mirror. Clean it every day, and let no dust gather on it.
Everybody was impressed. But a poor boy who worked in the kitchen, chopping wood, could not even read. He asked someone to read it to him... and then he asked them to write his answer.
There is no tree. There is no mirror. From the beginning, nothing exists. So where can the dust gather?
That kitchen boy became the next master. Because he saw that you don't have to clean the mirror all your life. You are not the mirror. You are the emptiness in which the mirror appears.
Osho taught: cleaning is good. But seeing is better. In one moment of seeing, all the dust is gone.
The Upanishads give a beautiful picture. Two birds sit on the same tree. Golden birds, the best of friends.
The first bird hops from branch to branch, eating the fruits. Some are sweet, and it is happy. Some are bitter, and it is miserable. Up and down, all day long.
The second bird sits on the highest branch, very still. It eats nothing. It just watches the first bird, with great love, and great peace.
Both birds are you. One part of you is always eating the fruits of life, sweet and bitter, happy and unhappy. The other part only watches.
And the moment the first bird looks up, and sees the second... it becomes still too. It discovers that it was always the same bird.
Osho taught: be the bird who watches. So go on eating the fruits, if you like. But now and then, look up.
There was a famous actor in a village drama company. Every year he played the part of a great king, with a crown and a sword and a long red cloak.
He played it so well, for so many years, that one day he forgot to take the crown off. He went to the market and ordered people about, as if he were the king.
People laughed at him. Then they became worried. Then they called a doctor.
We laugh. But every one of us is that actor. You are playing the part of a husband, a wife, a clerk, a Hindu, a Muslim, an Indian, a success, a failure.
Play the part. Play it well. There is nothing wrong in it. But remember, just under the costume... there is someone who is only watching the play.
Osho taught: life is a drama, and you are the witness. Then you can enjoy even the sad scenes. Because you know the curtain will come down... and you will still be there.
The Taoist master Chuang Tzu once dreamed that he was a butterfly. He was flying from flower to flower, happy, free, not knowing anything about Chuang Tzu.
Then he woke up. And there he was, lying on his mat, solid and unmistakably Chuang Tzu.
But he was puzzled. He said to his disciples: Now I don't know. Was I Chuang Tzu dreaming that I was a butterfly? Or am I a butterfly, dreaming now that I am Chuang Tzu?
The disciples laughed. But he was not joking. While you are dreaming, the dream is completely real. Only when you wake up do you know it was a dream.
So how do you know that this life, this morning, this body, these worries... are not another dream?
Osho taught: the witness is the one who wakes up. Dream or no dream, it is the one who sees.
Look at the sky in the monsoon. Black clouds come rolling in. Thunder, lightning, rain. It seems the sky has been destroyed.
And then the clouds go. And the sky is there, exactly as it was. Not a scratch on it. Not even wet.
Your thoughts are clouds. Your moods are clouds. Even your depression is a cloud, a big black one. And you... you are the sky.
The sky never fights with the clouds. It doesn't say: go away. It simply gives them space, and they pass.
So the next time a dark mood comes, don't say: I am depressed. Say: a cloud of depression is passing. And watch it pass.
Osho taught exactly this. It is a very small change in words. And it changes everything.
Somebody will ask: but if I am watching the mind, then who is watching the watcher? And who is watching that one? Will it never end?
It is a good question, a question of the mind. The mind always wants one more step. But the witness is not one more step. It is where the steps stop.
You can watch a thought. You cannot watch the watching. When you try, you simply fall into it, like a stone falling into a deep well.
And that falling is meditation. There is no more object, no more subject. Just pure seeing, without anyone who sees.
Don't try to understand this with the head. It cannot be understood. It can only be tasted, the way you taste sugar.
Osho taught: experience, don't believe. Nobody can describe the taste of sugar to you. Put a little on your tongue, and you know. So let us put a little on the tongue.

chapters.title: A Meditation: The One Who Watches

beats.say: Now let us sit, and simply witness, as Osho taught. Close your eyes. Let the body settle, like a glass of muddy water left on the table. Slowly the mud goes down.
Notice the sounds around you. Don't name them. Just notice. Sound comes... and goes. And you are the one who hears.
Notice the body. The weight on the floor. A little ache somewhere, perhaps. Feelings come... and go. And you are the one who feels.
Notice the thoughts. One thought, and another, and another. Let them come. Don't follow them. Thoughts come... and go. And you are the one who sees.
Now turn around. Look at the one who is seeing. Not with the eyes. Just rest your attention on the watcher itself.
You will find nothing there. No shape, no colour, no name. Only a silent, wide awareness. Rest in that.
This has always been here. Behind every thought, behind every tear. You are this.
Slowly now, take a deep breath, and open your eyes. And as you go into the day, now and then... remember the watcher.
